# SimpleSign — implementation reference

SimpleSign is a multi-targeted (`net8.0`, `net10.0`) .NET library for PAdES, CAdES and
XAdES signing and validation. It uses only platform cryptography and must remain safe for
Native AOT where the platform XMLDSig implementation permits it. This reference describes
the current source tree; use release-tagged documentation and `CHANGELOG.md` for the
behavior delivered in a particular package version.

## Signing contract

`AdesBaselineProfile` is the sole level configuration for PAdES, CAdES and XAdES:

```csharp
var profile = AdesBaselineProfile.Archive(
    new TimestampOptions(new Uri("https://tsa.example")),
    new LongTermValidationOptions(),
    new ArchiveTimestampOptions(new Uri("https://archive-tsa.example")));

var signed = await CadesSigner.Document(content)
    .WithCertificate(certificate, chain)
    .WithLevel(profile)
    .SignAsync();
```

Use `PadesSigner.Document`, `CadesSigner.Document` and `XadesSigner.Document`; logging is
always configured through `WithLogger`. All fluent builders are immutable. Credentials are
mutually exclusive: `WithCertificate` and `WithExternalSigner` replace one another.

`SignWithDetailsAsync` returns an `ISigningResult` with requested and achieved levels,
checked timestamp/LTV/archive flags and structured warnings. The completed base signature
and content integrity must verify before a result is returned. Strict success requires
`RequestedLevel == AchievedLevel`; `SignAsync` rejects best-effort profiles.
`ReturnLowerLevel` is available through the detailed terminal for enrichment failures,
while base-signature failures and cancellation still fail.

B-LT requires embedded issuers and applicable, authenticated OCSP/CRL evidence for required
non-root signer, prior-TSA, and responder paths. Cryptographically self-signed root
candidates and authorized OCSP no-check responders are exempt from their own revocation
objects. CAdES baseline LTV uses root CMS certificate/revocation sets and RFC 5940 OCSP
choices; validation also reads legacy CAdES-XL unsigned attributes.

## External signatures

Implement `IExternalSigner`. Its request contains the payload, resolved digest, signature
OID, payload kind, operation ID and PSS parameters. RSA and ECDSA results are verified against
the certificate before CMS/XML packaging. EdDSA signing is intentionally rejected while net8.0
cannot perform equivalent raw-output verification.

## PAdES-specific configuration

`PadesSignerBuilder.WithFieldOptions(SignatureFieldOptions)` atomically replaces field and
appearance configuration and is the explicit way to clear nullable field values. Batch and
deferred PAdES workflows use the same profile/provider/algorithm vocabulary as direct signing.

## Security rules

- RFC 3161 responses must bind to request OID, imprint, and nonce. Token integrity requires
  a matching TSA signer certificate, authenticated TSTInfo signed attributes, valid CMS
  signature, signing-certificate binding, and exclusive critical timestamping EKU.
- Evidence applicability and authenticity are distinct from signer-chain and TSA trust.
  Trust requires separate validation anchors and policy.
- TLS/TSA and revocation clients are supplied through `IHttpClientProvider`; callers retain
  ownership of their clients.
- CAdES/XAdES archive claims must be validated from final artifact structure and standards-defined
  preimages. Unsupported XMLDSig transforms or resources fail closed.
- Do not add cryptographic third-party packages, reflection-based serialization, dynamic code or
  unsafe code.

## Validation results

PAdES `SignatureValidationResult.Indication` is the single overall status:
`SignatureIndication.Valid`, `Invalid`, or `Indeterminate`. Integrity or cryptographic
signature failures and confirmed revocation are `Invalid`; an unavailable trust chain or
indeterminate revocation is `Indeterminate` when the cryptographic checks pass. Inspect
the individual checks and errors for the reason. PAdES results do not expose a parallel
`IsValid` boolean.

XAdES `DetectedLevel` describes observed unsigned-property elements, including properties
that fail validation. `HasValidSignatureTimeStamp`, `IsLtvDataValid`, and
`HasValidArchiveTimeStamp` report checked outcomes and must be inspected together with
base signature/integrity. `IsValid` combines fundamental signature, integrity, and
signer-chain checks. `IsTsaTrusted` separately reports signature-TSA trust.

## HTML to PDF

- Entry points: `HtmlToPdfConverter.Html(string|byte[])`, `.File(path)`, `.FileAsync(path)`, then the
  `HtmlToPdfBuilder` methods `WithStylesheet`, `WithPageSize`, `WithPageOrientation`, `WithMargins`,
  `WithTitle`, `WithAuthor`, `WithHeader`/`WithFooter` (`{page}`, `{pages}`, `{title}`, `{date}`),
  `WithFont(family, bytes[, FontVariant])`, `WithFontFile(family, path[, FontVariant])`,
  `WithBaseDirectory`, `WithResourceLoader(Func<string, byte[]?>)`, `WithLanguage`, `WithPdfA`,
  and `Convert`/`ConvertAsync`/`SaveTo`.
- Resources (images, stylesheets, fonts, SVG) are read only from data URIs, the sandboxed base
  directory, or the caller's loader. Do not add network access.
- Keep the engine dependency-free and AOT-compatible: no reflection, no `dynamic`, SVG via
  `XmlReader` with DTDs ignored and no resolver.
- Percentages inside `float` style values use the `CssLength` encoding (≤ −100000); never test
  `< 0` for "is percentage".
- Text in embedded fonts goes through `TextShaper` (GSUB/GPOS); measurement and drawing must use
  the same path (`TextMeasurer.UsesShaping`).
- Layout changes show up in `Snapshots/*.txt`; regenerate with `HTMLTOPDF_UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1`
  only when the geometry change is intended. Shaping changes must keep `ShapingReferenceTests`
  (HarfBuzz reference output) passing.

## Verification

Run `dotnet build SimpleSign.sln`, focused project suites beneath `tests/unit/`, CLI tests,
interop tests and the AOT smoke target before release. Cryptographic changes require positive
and negative artifact tests plus independent external vectors where available.
